name: Sydney
description: Central Sydney from open data, lit by the real sun. Every shadow is computed, and every height is traceable to its source.

water.note: Sydney Harbour is mapped as a water polygon (Port Jackson); the Overture ocean polygon stops at the Heads.

protection.title: Sydney LEP 2012, clause 6.18
protection.summary: Development may not add to the total shadow on these public places across their protected hours.
protection.source_note: Protected windows as amended by Amendment No 64. The NSW legislation site refused automated access, so they were transcribed from secondary sources; check the official text before relying on them. Places without a verified window show sun now but are not tested.
protection.reading_note: Two readings matter more than any data error. Times: the Standard Time Act 1987 is reported to read times in legal instruments as standard time, which during daylight saving is an hour later on the clock; for Macquarie Place that changes the sun in its window by up to 44 points. Baseline: the clause compares against buildings existing at a fixed date, while this test compares against today's model.
protection.tip: Tip: try the block west of Hyde Park, or just north of Martin Place.

reference_heights.source: Wikipedia, List of tallest buildings in Sydney (October 2026)

tour.title: Central Sydney from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap via Overture Maps, standing on NSW 5 m bare-earth terrain under NSW aerial imagery.

tour.title: Sydney Opera House
tour.text: Each shell is a spherical triangle cut from one sphere of radius 75.2 m, the rule Utzon settled on in 1961. The highest shell stands 67 m above sea level.

tour.title: Sydney Harbour Bridge
tour.text: Arch span 503 m, crown 134 m above sea level, 28 panels. The alignment comes from the two pylon footprints in OpenStreetMap, {landmark:harbour_bridge.bearing_deg}° east of north.

tour.title: A winter day on the towers
tour.text: 21 June, 8 am to 4 pm. The sun never climbs above 32.7° here, so at noon a 200 m tower casts a shadow over 310 m long.

tour.title: Martin Place at lunchtime
tour.text: On 21 June at 12:30, {sun:Martin Place|6-21|12:30}% of Martin Place gets direct sun; on 21 December, {sun:Martin Place|12-21|12:30}%. The plan protects it only from 1 September to 31 May, 12:00–14:00.

tour.title: Hyde Park in its protected hours
tour.text: Protected all year from 10:00 to 14:00. On the winter solstice, sun on the park falls from {sun:Hyde Park|6-21|10:00}% at 10:00 to {sun:Hyde Park|6-21|14:00}% at 14:00 as the towers to the west take over.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: surveyed, published or verified height. Orange: floor count × storey height. Green: estimated. Against {acc:matched} published tower heights the median error is {acc:median_abs_error_pct}%.

tour.title: After dark
tour.text: Windows light from the same facade grid that shades them by day. Drag to explore, or open Sun access to test a tower of your own.
